https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/foreign.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.27 15:00 Foreign Ministry proposes opening embassy in Brazil in October Translated by Justina Vaišvilaitė-Braziulienė Source: Elta EN Foreign Ministry proposes opening embassy in Brazil in October PHOTO: Audrius Gavėnas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google The Foreign Ministry has drafted a new government resolution proposing the opening of a Lithuanian embassy in Brazil on 1 October, revising an earlier plan to establish the mission in July. The embassy would be located in Brasilia, Brazil’s capital. Lithuania currently operates a consulate general in Sao Paulo. The ministry said the revised draft was prepared in line with the new government’s programme, which calls for expanding the network of diplomatic missions in countries and regions of strategic importance to Lithuania. According to a letter sent by the Foreign Ministry to the Finance Ministry, establishing and operating the embassy would require EUR 2 million in 2027, EUR 1.78 million in 2028 and EUR 1.36 million in 2029. In March, Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys told the politika.lt podcast that Lithuania needed an embassy in Brazil to better serve business interests and boost exports to Mercosur countries. He said the mission would provide an opportunity to expand Lithuania’s export markets. Source Topics It is forbidden to copy the text of this publication without a written permission from ELTA. https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/0.text: Experts are increasingly bullish on the potential of nuclear energy . Multiple Wall Street companies are predicting a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity for investors. "After decades of underinvestment, a convergence of generational technological breakthroughs, intensifying geopolitical competition, and the need for clean, dense, reliable power are positioning nuclear energy for a renaissance," predicts Goldman Sachs . Analysts at Goldman Sachs are particularly excited about relatively new forms of nuclear power, including small modular reactors, or SMRs. "[H]yperscalers have ... helped lead investment in the commercialization of next-generation nuclear power, namely small modular reactors (SMRs) and fusion energy ," the bank's analysts conclude. "These technologies, long brushed off as too far from commercialization, are now drawing significant public and private sector support." There aren't many publicly traded companies focused exclusively on developing SMR technology. However, there may be more on the way soon. The two most popular pure-play SMR stocks today are undoubtedly Oklo Inc. ( OKLO +1.03% ) and NuScale Power ( SMR +3.64% ) . Both have promising futures, but if you're looking for maximum growth potential, which one of these stocks is the more obvious choice? Both Oklo and NuScale are pursuing the development of SMRs, but each company's approach to doing so is very different. Oklo is focused mostly on building micro-reactors directly next to or near data center infrastructure. It is the data center build-out, a result of the rapid global adoption of AI technologies, that is driving power demand growth. Designing its systems to meet the exact needs of data center operators is, therefore, a reasonable go-to-market strategy. Oklo's strategy even caught the eye of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who invested in the company early. NuScale, on the other hand, is focused on supplying electricity to the grid through partnerships with major utilities. For example, NuScale is developing a 462-megawatts electric (MWe) SMR system in Romania. If built, it would be Europe's first commercial SMR. NuScale is also developing a 6-gigawatt SMR system in the U.S. for a major utility company. While Oklo and others are currently in the application process, NuScale is currently the only company in the U.S. approved by regulators to build an SMR facility. Image source: Getty Images. Here's the catch: Neither NuScale nor Oklo have ever actually built a commercial SMR system. Both companies have legitimate technologies, but application at scale remains just a theory. Whether their order books will translate into real market traction remains an open question, especially given that the SMR industry has seen massive project cancellations in the past. After a major customer canceled a NuScale project in 2024, for example, one industry report predicted that "no utility or government would invest another dime on these theoretical reactor concepts." In short, both Oklo and NuScale remain speculative investments despite having promising growth prospects on paper. After steep corrections, both companies have market caps well under $10 billion. The combined valuation of both entities right now is close to $10 billion. Nuclear energy, according to some analysts, will be a $10 trillion opportunity over the long term. Given the speculative nature of SMRs in general, investors may be better off including both Oklo and NuScale in their portfolios. Despite the downgrade, the airline says it is continuing normal operations and working to strengthen its finances. For years, airBaltic has operated on a financial knife-edge. The carrier has invested heavily in a fleet of new Airbus A220-300 aircraft and expanded its network, but those investments have yet to consistently translate into profits. The airline has posted annual losses in four of the past five years, with 2023 the exception. The picture has not improved this year. airBaltic reported a loss of 70 million euros in the first quarter, while its second-quarter results have yet to be released. Higher fuel prices following the war in Iran have added to the pressure, further weakening the carrierâs financial position. S&Pâs downgrade to CCC- puts airBaltic deep in speculative, or âjunkâ, territory. The rating indicates that the agency sees the airline as highly vulnerable to adverse business, financial and economic conditions and considers the risk to its ability to meet its financial obligations to be very high. S&P said airBalticâs existing cash and other financing sources are insufficient to reliably cover its upcoming financial obligations, leaving the airline dependent on external financing and support. The agency had previously supported its rating in part on the assumption that the Latvian government would provide assistance if needed. It now sees less certainty that government support would be sufficient or arrive in time. Uncertainty surrounding Latviaâs parliamentary election in October is adding another layer of risk. Airline seeks changes to bond terms airBaltic has also approached bondholders seeking changes to the terms of bonds due in August 2029, according to S&P. The airline is proposing to suspend cash interest payments for two quarters. Interest due in August and November would instead be capitalised, meaning it would be added to the outstanding debt rather than paid to investors in cash. The carrier is also asking for a temporary waiver of a requirement to maintain at least 25 million euros in cash in its bank accounts. That would allow it to use those funds for its operations. Because airBaltic is a state-owned company, government policy will play an important role in determining its future, Å imkus said. âIf it were not a state-owned company, the rating would probably be even lower,â he said. The Latvian government could assume additional obligations, while the airline could seek a strategic investor, potentially from one of Europeâs major airlines. âThe situation is not ultimately doomed, but the risks are high,â he said. airBaltic says it is operating normally In a response to LRT.lt, airBaltic emphasised that S&P is an independent credit rating agency and that its assessment is based on information available to it and assumptions applicable at a particular point in time. Photograph: Ukrinform/Shutterstock Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Russia Explainer Ukraine war briefing: Trilateral peace talks with Russia to restart, says Zelenskyy Ukraine will not discuss limits to its armed forces or enforced neutrality at November meeting, president says. What we know on day 1,706 Guardian staff and agencies Sun 25 Oct 2026 21.27 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A trilateral meeting between Kyiv, Washington and Moscow will take place in November aiming to restart stalled Russia-Ukraine peace talks, Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said . “We are ready to talk. If it’s a territorial issue, it must be addressed at a leadership level. Other issues fall within the remit of the technical groups. All this can therefore be discussed in November,” the Ukrainian president said on Sunday in an interview. Zelenskyy also renewed his push ⁠for a meeting between him and Vladimir Putin, believing that Putin is the only person ​in Russia who can make major decisions to end ​the war. Zelenskyy says that at the trilateral talks, Ukraine will not discuss limits to its armed forces, or enforced postwar neutrality . Kyiv has long sought entry into Nato despite the reticence of some members. Meanwhile, US warnings about imminent ⁠Russian ballistic missile strikes, critical to Ukraine’s air defences, have been fully restored , according to Zelenskyy. He told Ukraine’s ⁠TSN television channel that SpaceX’s ​Starshield satellite internet had been working at speeds of up to 420km/h since early on Saturday, after a meeting with the US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo. Starshield was throttled earlier in October amid diplomatic pressure on Kyiv from Washington. The US has been trying to pressure Ukraine to suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries , which it says push energy prices higher. However, Zelenskyy has repeatedly said Kyiv will only stop the strikes if Moscow stops hitting Ukraine’s power infrastructure, or if the US allows Ukraine to use of Starshield ‌over Russia to detect launch places of its ballistic missiles, or if it supplies Ukraine with Patriot missiles. Zelenskyy on Sunday said Russia had launched nearly 2,300 drones targeting Ukrainian cities over the past week , renewing his call on western allies to speed up deliveries of interceptors. “This week alone, Russia has launched about 1,600 guided bombs, 48 missiles of various types, including ballistic missiles, and almost 2,300 strike drones at Ukraine,” he wrote in an online post. Russia’s defence ⁠ministry said on ⁠Sunday ​its drones had struck a ⁠cargo vessel bound for the Black Sea port of ⁠Chornomorsk in an overnight ​attack ‌and another cargo ‌vessel en route to the ‌port of Odesa during the day. The ministry said the vessels were being used to supply the Ukrainian army. Russian ‌forces also hit a logistics centre, a ​distribution centre and a logistics terminal in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv overnight. Reuters could not confirm the reports. A Ukrainian drone attack overnight on the Russian border city ⁠of Belgorod killed ⁠three people ​and injured 13, local authorities said on Sunday , while ⁠a separate drone strike later in the day killed another person. The overnight attack on Belgorod ​damaged 30 apartment buildings, regional governor ⁠Alexander Shuvayev said. The presidential election in Bulgaria on Sunday ended inconclusively, with the next head of state to be picked in a runoff. In a surprisingly strong performance, the candidate of the pro-western reformist opposition, Andrey Gyurov, will face the incumbent leftist president, Iliana Yotova. Iotova opposes military aid to Ukraine and favours dialogue with Russia, while Gyurov has often expressed firm support for Kyiv . The vote was held amid security concerns after a series of drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea .
